### Observed differences

- The relative order of two sets of activities reversed. In the earlier window, A21 came before A30, A31 and A36, and A22 came before all three, in 100% of the 200 traces; in the later window the reverse order holds in about 995 of 1,000 traces for all six pairs, while every pair still occurs together in every trace in both windows. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- Relative positions moved accordingly: A30, A31 and A36 each shifted earlier (mean position from about 0.59 to about 0.41 of the trace), while A22 (about 0.38 to 0.47) and A21 (about 0.53 to 0.62) shifted later. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Control was handed off at different points. A20, which previously always passed to A22, in the later window passes to A30, A31 or A36 in roughly equal thirds (about 33 in 100 outgoing transitions each) and almost never to A22. A21, which previously passed to A30, A31 or A36 in roughly equal thirds, now passes almost always to A25 (about 995 in 1,000 transitions). The group members, which previously each passed to A25 in roughly a third of their outgoing transitions, now pass to A22 instead, and A25 is no longer reached from the group. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Overall, the earlier window reads A20 → A22 → A21 → {A30, A31, A36} → A25, while the later window reads A20 → {A30, A31, A36} → A22 → A21 → A25; the internal order of the three-activity group stays unfixed in both windows, each member being able to follow either of the others or to exit. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL001, REL004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that two segments of the process exchanged their order: the group A30, A31 and A36, previously executed after A22 and A21, is now executed before them, so the later window runs A20 → A30/A31/A36 → A22 → A21 → A25 where the earlier window ran A20 → A22 → A21 → A30/A31/A36 → A25; as part of this swap, A20 now feeds the group instead of A22, and A25 is now reached from A21 rather than from the group. The change is shown directly by the near-complete reversal of all six activity-pair orders with co-occurrence unchanged at 100% in both windows, by the matching position shifts of all five activities, and by the consistent successor changes at both ends of the swapped blocks; the 16 qualifying items are many times the roughly 0.34 expected by chance in the control-flow screening, and each item rests on all 200 traces per window. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

Limitations: the 16 items largely describe one underlying reordering rather than independent confirmations, and the evidence cannot distinguish a reordering within a single process variant from a flip in the shares of two pre-existing full variants, since each window shows essentially one dominant pattern; the internal order within the A30/A31/A36 group also remains unfixed, so the new sequence is not a single fixed path. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
